title: How a hole in the ground becomes a swimming pool

beats.text: If you carve a pool-shaped hole into a backyard, you have the start of a swimming pool.
The cut face reveals topsoil, clay, sand, rock, and the groundwater below them.
Next, a level bed of gravel spreads underneath the future floor and lets water drain.
A small valve seats in that floor so rising groundwater can enter safely. This is a relief valve.
Then hidden pipes connect the main drain and skimmer to a pump and return jets.
A steel grid forms the shell's skeleton. Concrete fired from a hose covers it. This is shotcrete.
Then you keep it wet for days, because concrete doesn't dry, it cures.
Smooth plaster covers the concrete, followed by waterline tiles, stone coping, and a ladder.
Now fill it: twenty thousand litres, about twenty tons of water.
A pump pushes it through a sand filter and back, the whole pool every six hours.
Add a ladder and some sun. Congratulations, you've built a pool.
